title: Bridging steady-state and time-domain descriptions of molecular electron transport
authors: Thibaut Lacroix, Namgee Cho, Clemens Vittmann, James Lim, Susana F. Huelga, Martin B. Plenio
abstract: Electron transmission from an input electrode, through a molecular system, to an output electrode has been widely studied using the steady-state non-equilibrium Green's function (NEGF) method. Recently, the wave packet method, which provides access to the transient dynamics of electrons as well as internal molecular degrees of freedom, has been employed to investigate enantiospecific electron transport through chiral molecules. In this work, we derive the quantitative relation between the transmission of a finite-size wave packet and the energy-resolved NEGF transmission, showing that the former corresponds to a spectral average of the latter weighted by the wave packet energy distribution. Exploiting this correspondence, we construct non-Gaussian auxiliary wave packets whose spectral weight encodes the Landauer energy-window, allowing current-voltage characteristics to be obtained directly from time propagation. We further show that the correspondence extends to spin-resolved transport in a spin-phonon model of chirality-induced spin selectivity.
summary: This paper establishes a quantitative link between the steady-state Non-Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) method and the time-domain wave packet (WP) approach for molecular electron transport. By showing that the WP transmission is an energy-weighted average of the NEGF result, the authors allow current-voltage characteristics to be calculated directly from time propagation. This consistency check is vital for accurately modeling complex phenomena like spin-dependent transport in chiral molecules.
main_problem: The paper addresses the theoretical challenge of connecting steady-state descriptions of electron transport (NEGF) with time-domain dynamics (Wave Packet method) in molecular junctions.
main_result: A quantitative correspondence is derived showing that the time-averaged transmission from the wave packet method equals a spectral average of the energy-resolved transmission calculated via NEGF.
method: The authors employ both the Non-Equilibrium Green's Function (NEGF) formalism for steady-state transport and the time-dependent wave packet propagation method for transient dynamics.
model_or_system: The system models electron transport through a molecular junction coupled to electrodes, extended to include spin-phonon coupling to study chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS).
key_observables: Electron transmission probability, current-voltage characteristics, and spin polarization.
important_parameters: Bias voltage (V), wave packet width ($\Delta$), and coupling strengths ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The correspondence holds for molecular tight-binding and spin-phonon models, and the analysis often assumes zero temperature.
figures_summary: Figures compare WP and NEGF results for total transmittance and spin polarizations, and show I-V curves derived from both methods.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the NEGF framework for steady-state transport, then introduces the WP method for time dynamics, derives the quantitative link between the two, and finally applies this equivalence to complex models like spin-phonon systems.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides a rigorous mathematical bridge between two powerful but distinct formalisms (steady-state vs. time-domain) used to study open quantum systems, which is crucial for understanding molecular electronics.
